derivation.device: adiabatic 1x2 mode-evolution power splitter (from Phase-A classification)

how_the_FoM_is_governed.split_balance: Structural: the geometry is mirror-symmetric about the axis, so the input fundamental excites only the SYMMETRIC supermode, which by symmetry deposits equal power in the two outer guides. 50/50 is guaranteed by construction, independent of platform. Predict 0.500.
how_the_FoM_is_governed.transmission_total: Adiabaticity + bend loss. Power stays in the fundamental supermode iff the taper evolves slowly vs the local supermode beat length L_beat = lambda/(2*dn); the bottleneck is the phase-match point (minimum dn). Radiation at the fan-out adds loss unless the S-bend radius >= min_bend_radius.

what_must_change_with_platform_and_why: 1) Guide widths -> single_mode_width_um (rule-based): center_input = arm_width = wg; all tips = min_feature. Wider, less-confined platforms need wider single-mode guides.

2) Coupling gap -> min_feature (strongest fab-allowed coupling => shortest adiabatic length). arm_offset = wg/2 + coupling_gap. With COMPLEMENTARY linear tapers (center wg->tip, outer tip->wg) the two widths sum to ~const, so center-outer edge gap stays ~= coupling_gap through the whole transfer and phase-match sits at w = wg/2.

3) Transfer (taper) length -> set from the LOCAL supermode coupling length at phase-match L_c = lambda/(2*dn) at (w=wg/2, gap=min_feature). Adiabaticity needs L_taper >~ a few x L_c. This is the platform-dependent scaling and is COMPUTED from mode solves, not guessed.
4) Fan-out S-bend -> sized so effective radius R_eff = 2*L^2/(pi^2*dy) >= min_bend_radius (bend radiation also cuts T).
5) Footprint kept within the per-stack budget (which scales with confinement).

iterations.reasoning: Moderate confinement. At full width L_c is huge (206um) but the transfer happens at intermediate widths: phase-match L_c(w=0.6)=25.5um. taper=100um = 3.9x L_c => adiabatic within the 150um budget. Fan-out R_eff=2*26^2/(pi^2*1.9)=72um >= 30um. Predict T~0.97.

tfln is the hard stack. Opening fully to gap=mf=0.5um makes Lc=64um -> only 1.6x adiabatic in the 150um budget (non-adiabatic). Compromise gap=0.30um (arm_offset 1.15): Lc=28.16um, 4.1x adiabatic, and larger gap than round-1's 0.25 so the 0.5um pinch tip is less merged. But gap 0.30 < mf 0.5 means still partly merged; the 0.5um min_feature tip is a hard Y-junction radiation floor in TFLN. Predict T~0.93 (improved from 0.84 but may fall short of 0.95 within budget).

Loss is gap/merging-dominated: opening gap 0.25->0.30 cut loss 0.160->0.070 (more than halved). This is my last call, so I spend it on the clear trend: open gap 0.30->0.35 (arm_offset 1.20). Lc rises 28->35um so adiabaticity eases 4.1x->3.4x (still comfortably adiabatic), while the 0.5um pinch tip is further un-merged. Extrapolating the loss trend predicts ~0.04-0.05 loss -> T~0.95 (right at threshold). If it still misses, the honest floor is: full unmerge (gap=mf=0.5) needs Lc=64um -> a ~200um device, over the 150um budget, so a >=0.95 clean-evanescent design is not reachable for TFLN's 0.5um min_feature within this budget.

final.floor_argument: The dominant loss is radiation from the center pinch-off tip in the partly-merged regime; the tip width is pinned at min_feature=0.5um (a hard fab floor). Un-merging (opening the gap toward mf=0.5) is the only clean cure, but at gap=0.5 the phase-match coupling length is Lc=64um, so >=3x adiabaticity needs a ~200um transfer -> a device well over the 150um footprint budget. Within 150um the gap can only open to ~0.30-0.35, where the empirical trend has SATURATED at T~0.93. Conclusion: T>=0.95 is not reachable for TFLN's 0.5um min_feature adiabatic 1x2 splitter within the 150um budget; 0.930 is the honest best. Balance is structurally exact (0.500-0.5075).
